note: 24 -> 25 on 2026-08-26 for mock-duet/g28-axis-set-from-model (GIT_102). NOT a regression: G28's axis handling carried no @invariant at all before — it checked a hardcoded ["X","Y","Z"] against the code's letters with no declaration, so this is a NEW invariant where none existed, not a dropped rung on an existing one. It lands at rung 4 because the mechanism with full coverage today is a source-text scan (test/gcode-derivation.test.ts) that reads the G28 case's own text for a quoted axis letter; TypeScript offers no barrier against writing `letter === "X"` again because `Om` is `Record<string, any>` throughout this package, so `axis.letter` typechecks against any string literal. The promotion recorded on the declaration is a branded AxisLetter type mintable only from a lookup in om.move.axes; that needs the OM typing tightened first, which is bigger than this fix. It comes off when that lookup type lands and the source scan becomes structurally unnecessary. Previously: 23 -> 24 on 2026-08-25 for shaping/the-shaper-to-restore-is-read-once-per-run (GIT_84). NOT a regression: that invariant has existed since GIT_59, at the same rung 5, with the same mechanism. It was excluded from the count because its declaration carried no @debt and so failed validation outright — an invalid declaration is not counted as debt, it is not counted at all. Making it valid is what made it countable, so this +1 buys back a row the ratchet had been blind to rather than admitting a new one. It comes off when the run's prior gets its own branded type, minted once at run start and required by Procedure.plan, which is the promotion recorded on the declaration. Worth noting what this episode says about the ratchet itself: a malformed declaration HIDES debt from the gate that exists to count it, and six of them hid this one for six merges. Previously: 22 -> 23 on 2026-08-23 for connector/clock-seam (GIT_43), a NEW invariant rather than a regression: the connectors' timers had no declaration at all before, they were simply written against the platform. It lands at rung 4 because the mechanism with complete coverage is a source walk (test/clock-fence.test.ts); the compile-time `declare const setTimeout: never` shadow on top of it is rung 7 but only in the files that carry it. It comes back off when the platform timers are made unnameable package-wide, which is the promotion recorded on the declaration. Previously: 21 -> 22 on 2026-08-21 for ui/unit-lengths, re-rated 7 -> 4. Nothing regressed there either: the lint is exactly as strong as it was, but it is a node:test that `pnpm build` never runs and no CI or hook runs for anyone, so 'build-failing' overstated it. That +1 is that honesty, not new debt, and it comes off the moment `pnpm test` runs on the path to main.
